report.summary: Both failures come from one root cause: GET /api/books and the /books page return every user's books, so the API test sees another user's book and the new-user UI test sees a non-empty table instead of the empty state. Fix the leak_books defect in app/main.py list_books first, and check why BUGS=leak_books is set in the environment that ran this build, since the CI workflow itself doesn't set it.

causes.title: list_books ignores owner_id when the leak_books bug flag is on
causes.explanation: app/main.py list_books() has a seeded bug: when "leak_books" is in BUGS it runs an unfiltered 'SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id' instead of filtering by owner_id. Both the JSON API (/api/books) and the server-rendered /books page call list_books, so each user sees every user's books. The API test creates a book as user A, then lists books as user B and finds A's id in the result. The UI test registers a brand-new user and expects an empty state, but the page renders a row 'From API-7c13d5e3 / Robot / Delete' that belongs to another user. The correct, non-leaking query (owner_id = ?) exists in the else branch, so the app is wrong whenever the flag is on and the tests are right to fail. The workflow file (.github/workflows/tests.yml) does not set BUGS, so the flag must come from the runner or the shell environment; that is the thing to verify.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:42: assert book["id"] not in other_ids -> AssertionError: assert 2 not in [1, 2]
tests\ui\test_login_ui.py:14: expect(books.empty_state).to_be_visible() -> Error: element(s) not found; Aria snapshot shows row "From API-7c13d5e3 Robot Delete" in the new user's books table
app/main.py:163-166: if "leak_books" in BUGS: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall() else: ... WHERE owner_id = ?
app/main.py:31: BUGS = {b.strip() for b in os.environ.get("BUGS", "").split(",") if b.strip()}
app/main.py:11: leak_books       GET /api/books returns every user's books
app/main.py:270 and 212-213: render_books and api_list_books both call list_books(user["id"])
.github/workflows/tests.yml:33-38: test step sets no BUGS variable
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the leak_books branch from list_books (or make it only apply in a dedicated bug-injection build) so the query always filters by owner_id. Then confirm the CI runner should not have BUGS=leak_books set, by checking the runner or repo environment settings and any .env files. Rerun the api and ui suites to confirm both tests pass.
